semantics.single_agent: all ICRA problems are single-agent; every recording is caused by agent x
semantics.room_visits: strict: every entry into a room of C_p is a story element (STAR §2.1; implied by the ICRA NFAs, whose room transitions read the room symbol). The key 'consistent_if_unreported_room_visits_allowed' gives the alternative reading.
semantics.start_end: story starts inside p1 and ends inside pn when the history is exhausted (ICRA §II-A)
semantics.repeats: consecutive repeated story entries (AA) = leave and re-enter the room (Fig. 5 self-loops)
semantics.occupancy: simplified history lists o twice: activation then deactivation
semantics.C_p: the map's rooms are fixed (Fig. 2 caption: C_p = {A..E}); derived stories using a subset keep the other rooms as reportable rooms
semantics.problem3: 'problem3_*' lets p' start/end anywhere (paper's w1, w6); 'problem3_anchored_*' forces p'_1 = p_1 and p'_last = p_n (§II-A)
semantics.problem2: interval cases 1..6 as printed (primes = sensor interval); see notes for the exact model

cases.source: derived (not in paper): tests the ICRA §III-B case-2 procedure (p. 4983) on the Fig. 2 map

expected.explanation: Case 2 (t0 < t0' < tf < tf'): agent goes A -> R1 -> B before tf, then after tf (story over) B -> R2 -> b1 -> R3 -> A -> R1 -> B -> R2 -> b3. The paper's procedure (run VALIDATEAGENTSTORY on (p_i..p_n) vs the whole s) forces p_n at the END of s and the agent inside p_i at t0', so it returns false.

cases.verified_by: independent BFS (not shipped; tests/oracles/brute.py is the shipped equivalent) with the four interval boundaries as explicit events (story constrains room entries only inside [t0,tf], sensors record only inside [t0',tf'], start/end anywhere outside); paper procedure = OR over suffixes of the strict checker

expected.explanation: No super-story exists (D is reachable only after b3; once on the A/B/C side after b4 the agent cannot reach D again). Printed lines 7 and 9 never add L(i-1, .), so L(n+1, m+1) is finite as soon as the last segment (p_n, j') -> F exists.

cases.source: derived (not in paper): tests the §V-B claim that a closest p' has length <= max{n, n'}

expected.explanation: L(M) = (A|C)*A B+ U B+ A (A|C)*. The only story at distance 1 from CCA is CCAB (length 4 > max{3,2}). The edit-count bound max{n,n'} does hold (1 <= 3).

cases.verified_by: independent lexicographic Dijkstra on (edits, length), not shipped, and brute-force enumeration of all accepted words up to length 6; 40/3000 random instances violate the length claim, 0 violate the edit-count bound

cases.source: derived (not in paper): tests the §V-B claim that a closest p' has length <= max{n, n'}, with a story that uses every room of the map, so the result does not depend on the C_p reading

expected.explanation: C_p = {A, B, C} is both the set of letters of p and the map's rooms, so this counterexample holds under either reading of C_p (unlike CCA, whose only closest story CCAB uses B, which is not a letter of CCA). Every accepted word starts with B: b1 (sides in R1, R2) must be crossed right after the first b2 crossing with no recording in between, which is impossible from R4, so the first b2 crossing goes R4 -> R2 and the agent starts in B, the only room of R4. Witness for BACB: B -> R4 -(b2)-> R2 -> A -> R1 -> C -> R1 -(b1)-> R2 -(b2)-> R4 -> B. The only story at edit distance 1 from ACB is BACB (length 4 > max{3, 3}).

cases.verified_by: independent oracle written separately from the fixture's first derivation (not shipped; tests/oracles/brute.py is the shipped equivalent): language of the history enumerated by depth-first enumeration of all walks with up to 10 room entries; strict consistency cross-checked by enumerating all interleavings of story and history; Levenshtein distance to every enumerated word (complete since n + d = 4 <= 10). Found by exhaustive search over Fig. 1 stories of length 3-5 using all three rooms and histories of up to 3 sensor events.
